_comment: Hand-maintained mapping from what the pricing page shows to what the API calls things.
Nothing here is inferred at runtime: no fuzzy matching, no lowercasing and hoping.
'page_name' is compared byte-for-byte against the data-name attribute of the model
card, and 'label' byte-for-byte against the row label inside that card. A page that
no longer contains these exact strings is a failure to report, never a row to guess at.
The keys of 'models' are API model ids. Several of them are ALIASES: today
mistral-medium-latest resolves to Mistral Medium 3.5, tomorrow it will resolve to
something else at a different price, with no change anywhere in this file. That is
precisely why the resolution is written down here by a human and revisited by a human.
Every id below was read off that model's own card at
https://docs.mistral.ai/models/model-cards/<slug>, which lists the versioned id and
its aliases together. They are NOT derived from the pricing page's card name, and
several would be wrong if they were: the card 'voxtral tts' is voxtral-mini-tts-latest,
and 'ministral 3 - 3b' is ministral-3b-latest, not ministral-3-3b-latest. When adding
a model, look its id up there rather than pattern-matching an existing key.
Last verified against the page by a human: 2026-08-04.
_comment_products: Nine entries below carry "kind": "product". The pricing page bills them beside the
models, but they are not models: they have no API model id, cannot be passed as a
model parameter, and are priced per call, per image or per month. Their keys are
descriptive slugs chosen here, NOT identifiers Mistral publishes, and they are the
only keys in this file that a consumer must not treat as callable model names.
'document-ai' is the second priced row of the same 'ocr 4' card that
mistral-ocr-latest reads its own row from. Two entries may share a page_name; rows
are matched by label within the card, so they do not collide.
_comment_voxtral: ASSUMPTION, revisit it. Both rows of the 'voxtral small' card carry the same
parenthetical, '(per min / per M tok)', and neither says which of the two units
applies to it. Reading the audio row as per-minute and the text row as per-M-token
is the sensible interpretation, and it is only an interpretation. It is written
down here, rather than inferred in code, so that a human can check it.
Note also that 'voxtral small' is billed in BOTH units at once: per minute of
audio in and per million tokens of text. Any code assuming one unit per model
Decoy on the page: 'voxtral mini transcribe realtime' carries a row labelled
'Audio Input/min' too, at twice the price of 'voxtral mini transcribe 2'. Rows
are read per card, never by searching the page for a label, which is what keeps
the two apart. Both are published, as separate models.
Nothing outside 'models' below is read by the scraper: this key is a comment,
_comment_absent: Three cards on the page carry no price at all and so have nothing to publish:
'leanstral', 'mistral moderation' and 'agent api'. They are deliberately absent
rather than published at 0 -- the page states no price for them, which is not the
same statement as a price of zero. Revisit when the page prices them.
